To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the induction of the c-myc and the c-fos genes is the result of an increased transcription and of a relief of a block to transcriptional initiation.
the c-myc gene is transcriptionally regulated during liver regeneration, while c-foss is transcriptionally regulated in the early phase and regulated post-transcriptionally in the late phase.
Transcriptional and post-transcriptonal control mechanisms are both involved in the regulation of c-myc expression during liver regeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control gene expression in the regenerating liver.
the molecular basis of the regulation of proto-oncogene expression during mouse liver regeneration, and with the mechanisms involved in transcriptional regulation in general.
understanding the molecular mechanisms which regulate the expression of proto-oncogen c-myc and fos genes in normal liver, and during liver regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the induction of c-mys and c-fos mRNAs in regenerating mouse livers involves both transcriptional and post transcriptional regulation.
the regulation of the proto-oncogen c-myc and fos during liver regeneration involves transcriptional and posttranscriptional mechanisms.

the c-myc gene is regulated by both post-transcriptional and transcriptional mechanisms in regenerating mouse hepatocytes, whereas the c-fos gene is predominantly under post-transcriptional regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

c-myc mRNA accumulation during liver regeneration is due to a relief of a block in transcription elongation, while c-fon mRNA accumulation is due to a combination of a relief of a similar block and an increased initiation of transcription.
c-myc is controlled mainly at the post-transcriptional level, while c-foss expression is regulated at the transcriptional level.

c-fos and c-myc are both induced in the regenerating mouse liver and the induction of c-fos mRNA is the result of increased transcription, whereas c-myc mRNA induction is the result of an increase in mRNA stability and a slight increase in transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transcriptional regulation of the c-myc and the c-fos genes during liver regeneration is more complex than previously thought, and involves both transcriptional and post transcriptional control mechanisms.
transcriptional and posttranscriptional mechanisms are not necessarily mutually exclusive.

c-myc mRNA accumulation is the consequence of both transcriptional and posttranscriptional mechanisms, and that the relative importance of each of these two processes is likely to be cell-type specific.
